title: FDA and EMA Endpoints and Pivotal Trial Designs for Endometriosis-Associated Pain Drugs
summary: Pivotal trial designs, pain endpoints, and responder definitions behind FDA endometriosis-pain approvals, compared with EMA authorizations and indication restrictions.
body_markdown:
## Endometriosis-associated pain: FDA-accepted endpoints and pivotal trial designs compared with EMA decisions


### Key takeaways


- The current FDA standard for endometriosis-associated pain comes from two oral GnRH antagonist programs. Orilissa (elagolix) was approved in July 2018[49](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=49) and Myfembree (relugolix/estradiol/norethindrone acetate) received its endometriosis efficacy supplement in August 2022[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=46)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=193) . Each rested on two replicate, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 6-month trials. Each used co-primary responder endpoints for dysmenorrhea (DYS) and non-menstrual pelvic pain (NMPP), and a responder had to reduce pain without increasing analgesic use[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=108)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115) .
- EMA has authorized two products for this use. Ryeqo (relugolix combination) gained the indication in October 2023[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=161) and Yselty (linzagolix) in November 2024[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=254) . Both used the same endpoint structure: DYS and NMPP responders, corrected for rescue analgesia, in 24-week or 6-month placebo-controlled trials[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=140)[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169) .
- The main differences between the agencies are the indication wording and the treatment-duration controls, not the endpoints. FDA labels cover "management of moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis" and set explicit maximum treatment durations driven by bone mineral density (BMD)[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=229)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=193) . EMA restricted both products to women with a history of previous medical or surgical treatment for endometriosis, placing them second line[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=156)[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=167)[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=197) .
- EMA accepted one pivotal trial (EDELWEISS 3) for linzagolix, supported by an extension. It approved only the 200 mg plus add-back regimen because the 75 mg regimen failed the NMPP co-primary endpoint[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169)[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=202)[204](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=204) .


### FDA: the GnRH antagonist-era evidence standard


#### Pivotal trial designs


Feature Orilissa (elagolix) Myfembree (relugolix/E2/NETA)


Pivotal trials EM-1 (M12-665, N=871) and EM-2 (M12-671, N=815)[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=64)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=87) SPIRIT 1/S1 (NCT03204318) and SPIRIT 2/S2 (NCT03204331)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=116)


Design Multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 6 months[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=64)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=87) Multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24 weeks[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=116)


Arms 3:2:2 placebo : elagolix 150 mg QD : elagolix 200 mg BID[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=64)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=84)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=87) 1:1:1 combination tablet for 24 weeks : placebo : relugolix 40 mg alone for 12 weeks, then combination for 12 weeks (delayed add-back)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=116)


Pain instrument Daily eDiary Endometriosis Daily Pain Impact Scale (0 to 3, severity and impact on daily activities), averaged over 35 days[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82)[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=62) Daily 11-point NRS (0 to 10)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=116)


Primary timepoint Month 3[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=63) Week 24, using the final 35 days of treatment[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=108)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115)


Entry pain criteria Composite Pelvic Signs and Symptoms Score of 6 or more, DYS and NMPP each 2 or more, NMPP on at least 4 of the prior 35 days[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=87) DYS NRS of 4.0 or more on at least 2 days, plus a mean NMPP NRS threshold during run-in[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=116)


#### Co-primary endpoint architecture


Both programs used two co-primary responder endpoints, DYS and NMPP. A responder had to meet both of the following[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=63)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=108) :


1. A prespecified reduction from baseline in the pain score.
2. No increase in analgesic use (NSAID or opioid) for endometriosis-associated pain.


The responder thresholds differed by instrument:


Product DYS threshold NMPP threshold


Orilissa EM-1 0.81-point reduction or more on the 0 to 3 scale 0.36 or more


Orilissa EM-2 0.85 or more 0.43 or more


Myfembree S1/S2 2.8-point reduction or more on the 0 to 10 NRS 2.1 or more


Orilissa thresholds are from[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82) . Myfembree thresholds are from[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=108)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=115) .


The elagolix thresholds were trial-specific. They were derived by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, anchored to the Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC)[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=63) .


#### Results that supported approval


Endpoint EM-1 150 mg QD EM-1 200 mg BID EM-1 placebo EM-2 150 mg QD EM-2 200 mg BID EM-2 placebo


DYS responders, Month 3 46% 76% 20% 43% 72% 23%


NMPP responders, Month 3 50% 55% 36% 50% 58% 37%


All elagolix comparisons with placebo were statistically significant[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=82) . For Myfembree, both co-primary endpoints were met in both trials[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=108) :


Endpoint S1 Myfembree S1 placebo S2 Myfembree S2 placebo


DYS responders, Week 24 74.5% 26.9% 75.1% 30.5%


NMPP responders, Week 24 58.5% 39.6% 65.9% 42.5%


The Myfembree key secondary endpoints were[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=108)[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=111)[114](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=114) :


- change in DYS NRS and NMPP NRS
- the EHP-30 pain domain
- dyspareunia NRS
- opioid use


#### What FDA reviewers said about the endpoints


The elagolix review record is the clearest statement of FDA's thinking on endpoints for this indication.


- **Co-primary endpoints and scales.** The Division found the co-primary DYS and NMPP endpoints acceptable. It considered the modified daily pain scales appropriate and found the cognitive-debriefing data supportive[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=86) .


- The Clinical Outcome Assessment reviewer judged the eDiary scales fit for purpose on face validity.
- The same reviewer noted that the submission had no evidence dossier on reliability, construct validity, ability to detect change, or cultural adaptation[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=77) .


- **Responder thresholds.** FDA accepted a responder framework but required the threshold to reflect a pain reduction that is clinically meaningful to patients[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=86)[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=81) .


- FDA treated ROC-derived thresholds as supportive, not preferred. It recommended anchor-based methods as the primary approach, supplemented by cumulative distribution function analyses[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=60) .
- Earlier reviewers stated that PGIC was "not a well-defined and reliable measure of endometriosis-associated pain in the proposed context of use"[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=75) .


- **Rescue analgesia.** FDA did not specifically endorse the sponsor's rule of a 15% or greater increase in rescue analgesic use. It stated that any change in rescue use counted against response should be clinically relevant[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=75) .


- In the Type A/SPA discussion, FDA said the primary framework should not use a mandatory analgesic threshold, although a threshold-based analysis could serve as a sensitivity analysis[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=75) .
- FDA still considered it appropriate to build rescue use into the responder definition and required labeling to say so[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=75) .


- **Dyspareunia.** FDA found dyspareunia efficacy only for elagolix 200 mg BID, and only at Month 3[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=89)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=92)[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=79) .


- FDA had encouraged the sponsor to rank dyspareunia higher in the testing hierarchy and to assess it through Month 6 to show persistence. The sponsor did not include Month 6 dyspareunia in the ranked testing[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=79) .


- **Opioid-sparing claims.** The 200 mg BID arm reduced opioid use at Month 6 with statistical significance, but FDA concluded that the mean reduction in opioid pills had not been shown to be clinically relevant[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=89)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=92) .


Drugs@FDA review text for the 2022 Myfembree endometriosis supplement was not retrievable. FDA's specific evaluation of the SPIRIT thresholds, and of any dyspareunia or opioid claims, therefore cannot be confirmed from the review record[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=193) .


#### Treatment-duration limits driven by BMD


FDA set dose-specific maximum durations based on bone safety:


- **Orilissa:** up to 24 months at 150 mg QD and up to 6 months at 200 mg BID[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=229)[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=209) .


- At 6 months, the decline in lumbar spine BMD compared with placebo was about 1% at 150 mg QD and about 3% at 200 mg BID[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=213) .
- Bone loss did not plateau. FDA expected 24 months at 150 mg QD to cause bone loss no greater than 6 months at 200 mg BID[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=213) .


- **Myfembree:** use is limited to 24 months because continued bone loss may not be reversible. The label recommends a baseline BMD assessment and annual BMD assessment for women treated for endometriosis[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=193) .


- At Month 6 in S1/S2, the least-squares mean change in lumbar spine BMD was -0.72% with Myfembree and +0.12% with placebo[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=182) .
- The label states that BMD changes beyond 24 months "have not been elucidated"[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=182) .


#### Legacy GnRH agonist programs


Older FDA-approved endometriosis products used a different evidence model.


- **Synarel (nafarelin):** compared with danazol 800 mg/day for 6 months. Efficacy was assessed as relief of pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea and dyspareunia, plus laparoscopic reduction of implants[239](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=239) .
- **Zoladex (goserelin):** two 6-month trials against danazol. Efficacy was assessed from symptoms, pelvic tenderness and induration, and laparoscopic lesion extent. The label noted that the clinical significance of lesion reduction was unknown[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=231) .
- **Lupron Depot add-back studies (M92-878, M97-777):** designed mainly around BMD. Efficacy was a secondary objective, measured with investigator- or patient-rated 4-point severity scores for five signs and symptoms[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=126) .


The move from laparoscopic lesion scores and investigator-rated signs to patient-reported daily DYS and NMPP responder endpoints is the main change between the GnRH agonist era and the GnRH antagonist era.


### EMA: Ryeqo and Yselty


#### Ryeqo (relugolix/estradiol/norethisterone acetate)


CHMP adopted a positive opinion on 14 September 2023 (procedure II/0013/G)[248](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=248) , and the extension was authorized on 30 October 2023[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=161) . The evidence was the same SPIRIT 1 and SPIRIT 2 program that supported the US approval. Both were 24-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with a delayed add-back arm[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=137)[147](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=147)[141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=141) .


- **Endpoints.** The co-primary endpoints were DYS responders (NRS reduction of 2.8 or more with no increase in analgesic use) and NMPP responders (reduction of 2.1 or more with no increase in analgesic use) at Week 24[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=140) . These are the same thresholds used in the US.
- **Results.** DYS responders were 74.5% compared with 26.9% on placebo in SPIRIT 1 and 75.2% compared with 30.4% in SPIRIT 2. NMPP responders were 58.5% compared with 39.6% in SPIRIT 1 and 66.0% compared with 42.6% in SPIRIT 2[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=134)[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=143)[138](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=138)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=133) .


- Dyspareunia NRS improved significantly in both trials[139](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=139)[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=145) .
- In SPIRIT 2, the analgesic pill-count endpoint was not met[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=145) .


- **CHMP view of endpoints.** CHMP considered the following acceptable[148](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=148) :


- an endpoint package focused on pain
- NRS as a validated pain measure
- separate DYS and NMPP measures, justified because treatment can cause amenorrhea
- a placebo comparator, even though dienogest is authorized in the EU, because placebo also allowed assessment of BMD effects


- **Long-term data.** Benefit was maintained through 104 weeks in an open-label extension[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=153)[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=160) .


- Mean change in lumbar spine BMD at Week 104 was -0.45%. Some women lost more than 5%[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=153)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=157) .
- The risk management plan lists "long-term use beyond 24 months" as a safety concern[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=157) .
- The product information recommends DXA scanning after one year of treatment[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=159) .
- The assessment material reviewed does not state a fixed maximum duration for endometriosis[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=153) .


#### Yselty (linzagolix)


CHMP adopted its opinion on 17 October 2024 (II/0013), and the European Commission decision followed on 22 November 2024[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=254) .


- **Pivotal design.** EDELWEISS 3 was the single pivotal trial: randomized, double-blind, double-dummy and placebo-controlled, with up to 6 months of treatment[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169) .


- The three arms were placebo (N=162), linzagolix 75 mg without add-back (N=160), and linzagolix 200 mg with add-back (E2 1 mg/NETA 0.5 mg) (N=162)[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=197) .
- EDELWEISS 6 was a supportive extension to 12 months[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169) .
- EDELWEISS 2 ended early (N=84), so it did not provide replication[204](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=204) .


- **Endpoints.** The co-primary endpoints were DYS and NMPP responders at Month 3, based on a 4-point verbal rating scale averaged over the last 28 days[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169)[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=202) .


- The thresholds were a reduction of 1.10 or more for DYS and 0.80 or more for NMPP, with stable or decreased analgesic use[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=202) .


- **Dose outcome.**


- The 200 mg plus add-back arm met both co-primary endpoints: DYS 72.9% compared with 23.5% on placebo, and NMPP 47.3% compared with 30.9%[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=202) .
- The 75 mg arm met the DYS endpoint (44.0% compared with 23.5%) but failed NMPP (38.9% compared with 30.9%, p=0.279). It was therefore not accepted for endometriosis[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=202)[201](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=201) .


- **CHMP comments.**


- CHMP noted that the composite responses were driven mainly by the pain-score components, because most participants had stable or reduced analgesic use[207](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=207) .
- CHMP accepted the Month 3 primary timepoint because onset was early and the effect was stable through Month 6[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=174) .
- Dyspareunia results were described as more modest (52.9% compared with 46.2% at Month 6)[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=206) .
- The sponsor did not seek CHMP scientific advice. It obtained national scientific advice from Sweden[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=177) .


#### The second-line restriction


EMA's main departure from FDA is the treatment population named in the indication. For both products, CHMP limited the indication to women with a history of previous medical or surgical treatment for their endometriosis.


- **Ryeqo.** In the phase 3 program, 98.6% of participants had used endometriosis medication before and 83.2% had had surgery. CHMP considered second-line use consistent with clinical guidelines[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=156)[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=158) . The assessment cites the ESHRE 2022 guideline, which treats GnRH antagonists as generally second line because hypoestrogenic effects limit how long they can be used[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=168) .
- **Yselty.** CHMP noted that guidelines do not recommend starting treatment with a GnRH agonist or antagonist because of BMD effects. The proposed indication was revised during assessment to match the EDELWEISS 3 population, in which 94% had prior surgery[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=167)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=174) .


No standalone EMA scientific guideline on endometriosis turned up in EMA's guideline collection. The EPARs describe the accepted evidence package, a 6-month placebo-controlled trial with rescue-adjusted DYS and NMPP responder endpoints plus extension data for durability and BMD, as the established approach rather than a codified requirement[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=168)[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=174) . No product-specific FDA guidance on endometriosis turned up either. The only related FDA guidance found was the general guidance on patient-focused clinical outcome assessments[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=94) .


### FDA compared with EMA


Dimension FDA EMA


Indication wording "Management of moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis"[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=229)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=193) "Symptomatic treatment of endometriosis in women with a history of previous medical or surgical treatment"[100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=100)[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=101)

### Implications for development programs


- **Endpoints.** Co-primary DYS and NMPP responder endpoints with an analgesic-use condition are accepted by both agencies. Separating menstrual from non-menstrual pain is needed because hypoestrogenic therapies cause amenorrhea[148](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=148) .
- **Threshold derivation.** Plan an anchor-based derivation of meaningful change with CDF support, and do not rely on ROC alone. Be ready to justify the anchor, since FDA questioned PGIC for this indication[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=60)[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=75) .
- **Rescue analgesia.** Avoid arbitrary percentage-increase rules in the primary definition. FDA wanted changes in rescue use to be clinically relevant, with any threshold handled as a sensitivity analysis[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=75) .
- **Replication and dose selection.** Two replicate trials remain the US precedent. The linzagolix case shows that each dose must meet both co-primary endpoints to be approved, and that one pivotal trial was accepted in the EU[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=202)[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=169) .
- **Bone safety.** BMD data out to 24 months drive the US labeled duration. In the EU, the lack of longer data is handled through risk management and monitoring[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=213)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=193)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=157) .
- **EU positioning.** A population that is mostly previously treated, which is typical of GnRH antagonist trials, should be expected to lead to a second-line EU indication[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=156)[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/endometriosis-associated-pain-fda-accepted?showSourceNumber=167) .
